title: Finite base field torsion cohomological dimension bound
statement: Let $K$ be a finite field. Every torsion abelian sheaf on the small étale site of $\operatorname{Spec}K$ has vanishing ordinary derived global-section cohomology in every degree greater than one. Equivalently, the torsion étale cohomological dimension of $\operatorname{Spec}K$ is at most one.

proof.text: Use the proved source etaleSheafEquivDiscreteModule and sheafHAddEquivGaloisH, from WeilConjectures.AlgebraicGeometry.Sites.GaloisModule, for the geometric stalk at a separable closure. The point torsion theorem makes the resulting discrete module elementwise torsion. These source results provide the sheaf/Galois equivalence and section/invariants comparison directly.

For each open subgroup U, infinite Galois correspondence identifies U with the absolute Galois group of its fixed field E. The extension E/K is finite, so E is a finite field. Transport constant-coefficient cohomology along E.fixingSubgroupContinuousMulEquiv (the proved source DiscreteModule transport lemma).

For each prime ell, if ell is zero in E, affine Artin-Schreier vanishing gives H²(Spec E, Z/ell)=0; the constant-sheaf Galois comparison gives H²(Gal(Ks/E), Z/ell)=0. Otherwise apply lem-sfb-finite-field-prime-degree-two. Hence constant prime degree-two cohomology vanishes on every open subgroup.

Apply the proved all-torsion version of the degree-two criterion, DiscreteModule.subsingleton_H_of_two_le_of_isTorsion in WeilConjectures.RepresentationTheory.DiscreteModule.Torsion. It extends the ell-primary criterion lem-sc-group-cd-one by the finite primary decomposition and finite-stable-submodule union, and shifts all higher degrees using the coinduced cokernel, which remains torsion. This is a generic devissage tool; the finite cyclic/inflation computation remains in the preceding prime degree-two lemma.

Transfer vanishing back to Sheaf.H. Apply nonempty_sheafH_extDerivedIso to identify its abelian-group-valued functor with ordinary derived global sections of the degree-zero sheaf. Unfold the torsion cohomological-dimension predicate; q>1 gives q≥2.
